concepts.def: Boundary where plates move apart and magma rises to create new crust; e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge produces Iceland's volcanism.
Boundary where oceanic plate subducts beneath continental; produces composite volcanoes and megathrust earthquakes (e.g. Nazca-South American).
Boundary where plates slide past horizontally; no crust created or destroyed but produces earthquakes (e.g. San Andreas Fault).
Logarithmic measure of earthquake magnitude based on seismic wave amplitude; each whole number is 10x larger amplitude.
Fast-moving cloud of hot ash, gas and rock from explosive volcano; killed 30,000 at St Pierre, Martinique (Mt Pelee 1902).
7.0 magnitude quake near Port-au-Prince killed around 220,000; example of LIC vulnerability with weak buildings and poor response.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Global Hazards — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Global Hazards brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Global Hazards.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is what type of plate margin?
options: Conservative
Constructive
Destructive
Collision

mcqs.q: At a destructive plate margin, what happens to the denser oceanic plate?
options: It subducts beneath the continental plate
It rides over the continental plate
It melts at the surface
It stops moving entirely
A fast-moving cloud of hot ash, gas and rock
A slow-moving river of lava
A flood of cold meltwater
A giant ocean wave

mcqs.q: Why did the 2010 Haiti earthquake kill so many people compared with similar-magnitude quakes in rich countries?
options: A bigger death toll always means the earthquake had a bigger magnitude.
Vulnerability - unreinforced buildings, dense informal housing, poverty and weak emergency services magnified the death toll, not just the magnitude itself.
Haiti's earthquake was magnitude 9.5, the largest ever recorded.
The Richter scale measures wind speed.

mcqs.q: Is flowing lava the main killer in volcanic eruptions?
options: The Richter scale measures wind speed.
Lava flows are the deadliest volcanic hazard.
Volcanoes are dangerous mainly because of their loud noise.
No - lava usually moves slowly enough to escape; pyroclastic flows, lahars and ash cause most deaths because they are fast, hot and far-reaching.

mcqs.q: Is a magnitude 6 earthquake twice as powerful as a magnitude 3?
options: The Richter scale measures wind speed.
No - the scale is logarithmic: each whole number is ten times the wave amplitude and roughly 30 times the energy, so a 6 is vastly stronger than a 3.
Magnitude is a linear scale, so 6 is double 3.
Volcanoes are dangerous mainly because of their loud noise.
